checks.name: Authenticated seeded browser matrix
checks.scope_rationale: Scoped to public launch on 2026-07-28. The owner has walked the signed-in product in production — signup, login, Stripe trial, access, cancel, AI generation and lifecycle email — and it works (docs/evidence/2026-07-28-owner-production-walkthrough.md). Calling the core journey unproven after that would be the gate wrong in the cautious direction, which is still wrong. What the matrix adds over one person clicking the happy path is phone and keyboard operation, cross-account isolation driven in a real browser, and the failure paths (session expiry, provider timeout mid-generation, reload during export). A supervised cohort of invited accounts with the owner watching can absorb those; strangers arriving unannounced cannot. So it stays required for public_paid.

owner_evidence.title: AI_SPEND_DAILY_CEILING_USD set in production
owner_evidence.note: 2026-07-28: owner set AI_SPEND_DAILY_CEILING_USD = 15 (first set to 5, then reconciled). Recorded as `configured`, not `observed`: nobody has run release:check in the production environment to confirm the value is live there. What this variable is: an ALARM only, read by /api/admin/readiness to compute spend_over_ceiling. It does not stop generation. The brake is MAX_AI_CALLS_PER_DAY = 300 (a single global pool, not per account), which at ~$0.044 per claude-haiku-4-5 call permits roughly $13/day — so a 15 alarm sits just above what the brake can physically allow, and the two now agree. The cap was deliberately NOT lowered to 120: it is global, so a tight value fails closed on paying customers during a busy day. Per-account cost is bounded by backend/lib/plan-limits.js, which is the real economic control (starter 30 actions ~= $1.32 on $12.99, pro 120 ~= $5.28 on $24.99, studio 400 ~= $17.60 on $59.00 — 70-90% gross margin).

how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".
3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.
Any commit after step 2 creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO.
